task: Fix the broken pagination after the cursor was not URL-encoded in the response.

candidate_memories.content: Pagination fails for records with special characters in the sort key because the cursor is not URL-encoded.
The pagination cursor must be base64-encoded before inclusion in the response to handle all sort key values.
The cursor was changed from opaque base64 to a plain-text format in the last sprint for easier debugging.
Pagination works correctly for records with alphanumeric sort keys; only special characters cause failure.
Session 2 note: the QA team documented pagination failures for product names containing ampersands and hash characters.
The API uses cursor-based pagination for all list endpoints to support large result sets.
Session 6 note: the API team added documentation for the cursor pagination contract.
Old practice: the cursor was an opaque token from the beginning to allow the server to change its encoding.
The cursor encodes the sort field value and the record ID to support stable pagination under concurrent writes.
Session 11 note: a client reported pagination failures for product names with forward slashes.
Old cursor guide: base64 encoding was chosen to prevent clients from parsing cursor internals.
Pagination cursors must be opaque and encoded to prevent clients from depending on their internal format.
Session 4 note: the API team ran a cursor stability test across 1,000 concurrent pagination requests.
The cursor has a 24-hour validity window after which it is rejected and pagination must restart.
A pagination regression test in session 8 confirmed all standard ASCII sort keys paginate correctly.
The list endpoints support sorting by name, created_at, and updated_at.
When changing cursor encoding formats, maintain backward compatibility for in-flight pagination sessions.
Session 9 note: the debugging team used the plain-text cursor format to trace a pagination bug.
Old pagination guide: the plain-text cursor was introduced as a temporary debugging aid.
Mobile clients cache the cursor for offline pagination and send it in subsequent requests.
